**Goal:** use the same Linux, SSH and Git skills on a Raspberry Pi, then build an elementary 3.3 V digital input/output circuit.

## Required Raspberry Pi mini-project

1. On a teacher-approved Pi, image Raspberry Pi OS, verify login, connect to an approved network and test SSH.
2. Review the GPIO pinout. **GPIO uses 3.3 V logic.** Never put 5 V directly into a GPIO input, connect a motor directly or experiment with mains electricity.
3. On an unpowered breadboard circuit, wire an LED through a suitable current-limiting resistor to a permitted GPIO and a button to another GPIO with an appropriate pull-up or pull-down arrangement.
4. Use [GPIO Zero](https://gpiozero.readthedocs.io/) in Python to blink the LED and read button state.
5. Read and log Pi CPU temperature and timestamp to CSV with an approved Python script, then use a defined condition to switch an indicator LED. The button may mark events in the log.
6. Commit working code, a wiring diagram and a short results paragraph to your GitHub portfolio.

For physical circuit work, require a teacher wiring check before powering.

## Simulate first

- [Wokwi Raspberry Pi Pico simulator](https://wokwi.com/pi-pico) is an accessible place to build and test simple LEDs, buttons and MicroPython code. **Pico is a microcontroller**, not a full Raspberry Pi running Linux. Code written for MicroPython on the Pico is not identical to full-Pi GPIO Zero code.
- [PiForge](https://getpiforge.com/) advertises a browser-based Pi-style virtual computer and GPIO environment. This is newer software: test compatibility, access, privacy and availability on school machines before using it for assessment.
- [Velxio Pi 4 simulator](https://velxio.dev/raspberry-pi-4-simulator/) offers Pi 4-style GPIO/Python emulation but its free access is limited. Confirm access before relying on it in class.

The retired Microsoft Raspberry Pi web simulator is not recommended as the primary classroom option. None of these should replace testing code and wiring on real hardware when available.

## Extension choices

Add an approved environmental sensor, compare thresholds, graph data, show a status page locally or build a simple enclosure. Any hardware-measurement challenge requiring additional equipment belongs in the [Engineering Preparation Track labs](../engineering-preparation-track/labs/index.qmd).
